column3: “plainly says” renders an emphatic doubled verb.
“to God” renders “to ha-Elohim,” which may refer to God or to the judges; “permanently” renders “forever.”
“because of his unfairness to her” renders “because he has dealt treacherously with her.”
“conjugal rights” renders a rare word (onah) whose meaning is uncertain.
“shall surely be put to death” renders an emphatic doubled verb (also in verses 15–17).
“remains in bed” renders “falls to a bed.”
“his loss of time” renders “his sitting,” and “take care of him until he is completely healed” renders a doubled verb, “healing he shall heal.”
“he shall be punished” renders a doubled verb, “avenged he shall be avenged.”
“he survives” renders “he remains,” and “his property” renders “his money (silver).”
“she has a miscarriage” interprets “her children come out”; NASB adds “further” to “injury,” and “as the judges decide” renders an uncertain phrase, “by the assessment.”
NASB adds “further” to “injury”; “appoint as a penalty” renders “give.”
“shall surely be stoned” renders an emphatic doubled verb.
